gaps: P0: no candidates. P2: only #6, a copy of the 1642 La Brière profile with an unreliable 1742 date. P3: only an organ-case drawing (#7).
notes: #3 and #5 are the same Beaulieu/Collignon 1642 siege plate (#3 on a two-page spread, #5 with an ornamental border); the city is a distant speck behind siege troops, so the La Brière drawing was preferred for P1. #2 and #4 are blank pages. #8 is small (about 1150 px wide after trimming) and dated only 1880–1910. #13 is a Fantin-Latour painting in the city museum, not a view.
